reason: The opcodes and the routine's own counts check out: 59 bytes against 51 (+8), the non-player path saves 3, the no-wrap and wrap stores save 1 each, and it assembles. But the +8 bytes move everything from move_mover_right (&1FFC) to the next absorbing SKIP. The SKIP 2 at line 3388 cannot absorb 8 bytes, so the shift runs on through the hot search loop. I assembled base and candidate in scratch (same flags as the Makefile's shipping build) and diffed the listings' branch page crossings. Ten branches change. The costly one is in the target search loop: stf_left_test_s moves from &27F8 to &2800, so 'BCC search_prefilter_next' at &27FE (window line 4035: 27.9 cycles over about 10.9 executions a pass, so about 6 taken) now crosses from page &28 back to &27. That is +1 on each taken branch, about +6.1 cycles a pass. 'BNE stf_left_test_s' at &27F7 now crosses too (about +0.3). 'BRA um_populate' now crosses (+1 a pass), and replot_player, update_player_in_exploding_helicopter and projectile_hit_player start crossing as well. Against these, only not_throwing_grenade, move_helicopter_towards_target_vertically and calculate_bullet_screen_address stop crossing (under 1 cycle a pass). That is roughly +7 cycles a pass of new crossing penalties against the claimed 6.29 saved: no net gain, probably a loss. The relies_on also says no branch inside the routine crosses a page, which is wrong. The out-of-line player block sits at &1FFA-&2003, so 'BMI skip_animation' at &2000 and 'BRA am_common_e3fb' at &2002 cross back to page &1F (+1 each when taken). The player-in-a-helicopter path is +3 slower than before, not +2.
